newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- New Aspiration's internal conflict has eased after secretary-general Sanoh Thienthong appeases MPs of the so-called August 17 group. The interior minister has promised them projects initiated by Sukhavich Rangsitpol while he was education minister, including his reform and computer acquisition programmes, would not be axed. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- A Burmese prisoner accused of involvement in an attempt to assassinate the ruling junta's intelligence chief has appealed to the government not to send him back to Rangoon. San Naing makes his appeal from Bangkok Special Prison amid concerns the government is under pressure to hand him over to repay Rangoon for returning drug fugitive Li Yun-chung. (BANGKOK POST)

- After an extensive investigation, a group of doctors has found unusually high levels of lead in the blood of primary schoolchildren in two southern provinces as a result of high concentrations of lead from abandoned tin mines in water, sediment and soil in parts of the Pattani River basin. The doctors now fear that the health and behaviour of the children could be affected. (THE NATION)

- Deputy Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra has indicated that the Eighth National Economic and Social Development Plan might have to be changed. Thaksin says Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has told him to supervise development projects that required close cooperation with the National Economic and Social Development Board. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Customs Department will lower the cash guarantee on payments of import duty for export-oriented industries with an aim to relieve the financial burden on exporters. Manufacturers who produce for export are currently required to deposit 50 percent in cash of the import duty on raw materials before a tax refund is completed. (BUSINESS DAY, THE NATION)
